answer: Juniper Routing Quotient. Each agent's routing weight equals the graph conductance of its neighbors-of-neighbors; an oasis of mutually-linked fresh nodes shares one small conductance pool. Enforced by capping credit per pool, not per key, so cloned identities split rewards rather than multiply them. An attacker pays the umber cost of building many distinct, credibly independent neighborhoods with real latency and upkeep, roughly N times the edge-formation work per identity.
